title: Become a Senior Consultant at Deloitte Finance Transformation
description: What can you expect as a consultant at Deloitte? In the role as a Senior Consultant, you will work together with our clients in developing their finance function. This involves a wide range of tasks; from optimizing daily operations to developing finance strategies for the finance function of the future. In the role as a Senior Consultant, you will work closely with other experienced colleagues and by knowledge sharing and continiously improvement in how we work, make great solutions for the challenges our clients are facing. At Deloitte, learning and development is one of our highest priorities. You will therefore be assigned a Talent Manager when you start, who, among other things, will help frame your everyday life and ensure that this can align with your private life and your goals for professional development. No two career paths at Deloitte are the same, so whether you want to become a specialist, the CFO of the future or something completely different, we are ready to help you get there. In addition, you will participate in an internal training program that is based on your experience and skills. The Consulting Academy focuses on preparing you for the work as a senior consultant, while the Finance Transformation Academy is tailored for consultants who will work with accounting and financial tasks in everyday life. We work from both Copenhagen and Aarhus, which is why the position can be filled from both locations. Exciting tasks await you From your first day at work, you will work as a consultant at our clients. Based on the client's needs and your experience and skills. The tasks will typically involve: Assisting and advising client's finance and accounting functions Optimization of core processes within finance and accounting KPI and management reporting using e.g. Power BI Development of methods or models that streamline the client's everyday life or can form the basis for strategic decisions Data analysis and processing in, for example, Excel, VBA or Python Transforming the finance function and developing financial strategies Implementation of new systems, such as ERP systems. You get the opportunity to shape your everyday life, and we make a great effort to match you with the right tasks, based on your skills and preferences. You have the following skills and experience We are looking for candidates who identify with the qualities listed below, who are passionate about strengthening our ability to help our clients improve their finance functions. You have a Masters degree such as cand.merc.aud or similar and have 2-6 years of experience as an auditor Most importantly, you want to make a difference for our clients. Come with your perspective on what you can contribute – and we will be happy to listen. You have analytical skills and an interest in accounting, processes and financial management, as we help our clients solve problems that they cannot solve alone. It is important that you feel comfortable working with other people, are able to put yourself in other people's shoes and understand that there may be different interests that needs to be met. Your everyday life will place great demands on your social skills, ability to communicate clearly and effectively across different levels in the client's organization and internally at Deloitte.

title: Assistant Manager/Manager, Traded and Quantitative Risk — CCR/CVA
description: Connect to your Industry Counterparty Credit Risk (“CCR”) and Credit Valuation Adjustment (“CVA”) Risk are major risk types for Financial Institutions, particularly within the Capital Markets divisions of banks and other financial institutions that trade derivatives, securities financing transactions and other counterparty-facing products. These risks sit at the intersection of front office, risk management, finance, model risk, collateral management and regulatory capital. CCR and CVA capital can represent a material component of a bank’s prudential capital requirements, particularly for institutions with significant derivatives and securities financing activity. The drivers of CCR and CVA are complex, requiring a detailed understanding of traded products, counterparty exposure, collateralisation, netting, margining, wrong-way risk, exposure modelling, and the regulatory capital frameworks used to measure and manage these risks. As we expand our Risk Advisory business to more holistically include all risk types, the focus on CCR and CVA continues to increase. With important regulatory developments including SA-CVA, SA-CCR, advancing IMM expectations and model risk management expectations for counterparty credit risk, client-driven demand to support banks and other financial institutions in these areas is creating an increasing need for these skills. Máš povědomí o korporátních financích , finanční analýze , modelování , financování a cash flow . Pokud máš k tomu i nějaké praktické zkušenosti, velmi to oceníme. Šikovné nováčky do dvou let povýšíme na seniora a v tu chvíli se jim zvedne plat klidně o 20 000 korun. Na příjemné benefity budeš mít nárok už od začátku. title: Associate Director - People in Deals - Centre of Excellence
description: Job description As a firm we help our clients navigate their biggest issues and opportunities. We aim to be universally recognised as a great place for great people to do their best work – a firm known for our collaborative and inclusive culture. And we will take pride in driving lasting, positive change in society. KPMG's Commitment to Inclusion: We are proud of the value we place on individuality; we want you to bring your full self to work and truly maximise your potential. We believe that your individuality helps us to deliver the best results for our clients. Diversity of background, diversity of experience, diversity of perspective - that's the KPMG difference. KPMG research shows that 2/3 of deals fail to deliver value, and amongst the top reasons are People and Culture. HR M&A was set up as part of the Integration & Separation (I&S) team in Deal Advisory, which has been growing year on year and seen by our clients as a market leader. We have worked on some of the largest and most high-profile client engagements in the deals space, including multi-billion spins, integration of global mega mergers, disposals of non-core assets for large multinationals. We have launched a market differentiating digital engagement platform for M&A as well as a campaign focused on ‘the Human Side of Deals’, and we continue to drive digital innovation. This is an opportunity to be part of a fast growing, dynamic, working flexibly, collaborative culture and diverse team, made up of HR deals professionals working alongside with deal execution teams on large scale, global integrations, separations and Joint Venture, across a range of sectors (Financial Services, Healthcare, Real Estate, Consumer, Industrial, Technology, Media and Telecommunications or Business Services). We work together to develop solutions to the issues our clients may face and understand the financial benefits or risks that may be present from a people perspective. Above all, you will be able to demonstrate how you can live our KPMG values: - Integrity: We do what is right. - Excellence: We never stop learning and improving. - Courage: We think and act boldly. - Together: We respect each other and draw strength from our differences. - For Better: We do what matters. At KPMG, our values define who we are and the way we do business. The Associate Director role is a key role to the team, developing our practice and proposition areas, leading, and delivering global projects, and working alongside the C-suite of global organisations. As one of the most successful teams in KPMG, we believe heavily in the development of our people. Associate Directors will work alongside Partners and Directors, providing one to one coaching as well significant internal and external courses, and performance management, to help develop them and rapidly build their careers. We advise on all aspects relating to HR and change management on the deals process from HR due diligence through to deal execution. Our focus areas: 1) Employee experience: Shaping the employee experience strategy and executing an engagement program. This often is based on our unique digital engagement platform, to ensure that the workforce is engaged, and key talent is retained in order to protect deal value 2) Organisational Design: Organisation Design, people strategy, operating model, driving synergies and value enhancements for integrations, carve-outs, or Joint Venture. Managing the talent risks and retention strategies, putting in place the strategy and execution programme to stand up Combined Company 3) Labour relations and compliance: Ensuring that labour and HR risks and obligations are understood and managed globally in order to deliver on the deal timelines and planned changes. We have one of the strongest experiences in workforce transition in the market. 4) HR operations: HR Operations focuses on the integration of the HR function itself, from strategy, operating model, integration or separation of systems and processes including standing up/securing payroll on deals. Our wider Integration & Separation (‘I&S’) deals team culture and HR M&A ways of working are highly collaborative, open, and high performing. Associate Directors are not expected to have all skill sets, but to lead teams to deliver on these areas. Responsibilities You will be responsible for leading client delivery and supporting practice development for the Technology in M&A team. title: Guidewire Test & Delivery Lead Senior Manager

This role combines end‑to‑end testing leadership with broader delivery oversight, working closely with business stakeholders, technical teams, and third‑party vendors to ensure high‑quality, predictable outcomes.

You will be responsible for defining and executing the testing strategy while also contributing to overall programme delivery, governance, and risk management across Guidewire implementations.

What your days will look like:

Testing Leadership

  • Own and drive the end‑to‑end testing strategy across Guidewire implementations, including functional, integration, UAT, non‑functional, and regression testing. Lead test planning, design, execution, defect management, and reporting across multiple delivery phases. Ensure alignment of testing activities with programme milestones, delivery plans, and release schedules.

  • Establish and maintain quality standards, test governance, and entry/exit criteria. Oversee test environments, data readiness, and defect triage with delivery and technical leads. Manage onshore and offshore testing teams, including test leads, manual testers, and automation resources.

Contribute to delivery planning, dependency management, and cross‑workstream coordination. Provide clear, confidence‑building status reporting to senior stakeholders and leadership. Support mobilisation, go‑live readiness, and post‑deployment stabilisation activities.

Stakeholder & Vendor Management

Act as a key interface with Guidewire and other vendors, ensuring responsibilities and support boundaries are clearly defined.   • Experience working with onshore and offshore teams, including third‑party vendors.

  • Strong understanding of delivery risk, governance, and quality management within large programmes contributing too excellent stakeholder management, communication, and leadership skills.

​
